verdict.summary: Composio has no managed Pipedrive OAuth app, so you have to bring your own. A private app in Developer Hub can go live straight away and be installed by any Pipedrive company through an unlisted link, with no review. Only a public Marketplace listing goes through review, which can take up to 21 business days.
verdict.hands_on_effort: 30-60 min for a private app; 1-3 days of prep (listing, legal pages, demo video) if you want a public Marketplace listing
verdict.approval_wait: none for a private app; up to 21 business days for a public Marketplace app

gates.name: Draft app (developer sandbox)
gates.unlocks: You can install and test the app with 'Install & test' and authorize your own sandbox company through Composio.
limits: Needs a developer sandbox account set up with 'I'm building an app that integrates with Pipedrive'
Draft private apps can only be shared with users in the same Pipedrive company
Only one callback URL per app
Access token lasts 60 min; refresh token expires after 60 days without use

gates.name: Live private app (unlisted installation link)
gates.unlocks: Any user or company in Pipedrive can install the app through a direct, unlisted installation link. No Marketplace review is needed.
limits: Pipedrive checks the callback URL when you click 'Change to live', so it must already work
A live private app can't go back to draft
The app type (private or public) can't be changed later
Rate limits apply per Pipedrive company account (third-party sources)

gates.name: Public Marketplace app (approved and published)
gates.unlocks: The app can be listed and found in the Pipedrive Marketplace. A live private app's link already works for anyone, so you only need this gate if you want a Marketplace listing.
limits: Must be created as a public app, because a private app can't be converted
Requires agreeing to the Developer Partner Agreement, plus a Terms of Service page, a Privacy Policy page, a demo video explaining scope use, working test accounts and a contact person
Approved apps are unlisted by default until you click 'Publish'
gates.time_to_reach: Up to 21 business days of review, plus prep time

steps.title: Sign up for a Pipedrive developer sandbox account
steps.detail: Go to developers.pipedrive.com and sign up for a Sandbox Account. When asked, choose 'I'm building an app that integrates with Pipedrive', because this is the option that gives you Developer Hub.
gotchas: Without a sandbox account set up for app building, Developer Hub doesn't appear.

steps.title: Open Developer Hub
steps.detail: In the sandbox account, go to Settings > (your company name) > Developer Hub.

steps.title: Create a private app
steps.detail: Click 'Create an app' and pick the private app option. This is the fastest route for Composio: there's no review, and you can share it with any company through an unlisted link. Choose 'Create public app' only if you plan to list on the Marketplace.
gotchas: You can't change the app type later in Developer Hub. A Marketplace listing would need a separate public app.

steps.title: Fill in Basic info with the Composio callback
steps.detail: The Basic info tab has two required fields: enter an App name and the OAuth Callback URL, then click Save.

values.label: Redirect URI
values.value: Composio callback URL (see the Composio callout on this page)

gotchas: Pipedrive allows only one callback URL per app, so enter exactly the URL your Composio auth config shows. Composio sources list two possible URLs (/api/v1/auth-apps/add and /api/v3/toolkits/auth/callback).

steps.title: Select access scopes
steps.detail: On the 'OAuth & access scopes' tab, set 'Access scopes (required)'. At minimum, match Composio's defaults. Scopes are fixed on the app rather than sent in the authorize URL, and users accept or deny all of them together.

values.label: Scopes
values.value: contacts:full, leads:full, mail:full, activities:full, products:full, projects:full (add deals:full etc. if your agent needs them)

gotchas: Changing scopes in Composio does nothing. Edit them on the app in Developer Hub.
Avoid 'admin' unless you really need it: it grants broad admin rights, and reviewers check that every scope is necessary.

steps.title: Copy the client ID and secret into Composio
steps.detail: The 'OAuth & access scopes' tab shows the client_id and client_secret after you save. Create a Composio auth config for the pipedrive toolkit using OAuth2 with your own credentials, and paste both values in.

steps.title: Install & test with your own account
steps.detail: Click the green 'Install & test' button, or start a Composio connection, which sends you to https://oauth.pipedrive.com/oauth/authorize with your client_id and redirect_uri. Confirm the callback succeeds and a test API call works against the api_domain returned in the token response.
gotchas: The authorization code expires after 5 minutes.
If the client_id is invalid, Pipedrive returns a 401 JSON error instead of redirecting.
The access token expires after 60 minutes, and the refresh token expires after 60 days without use.

steps.title: Switch the private app to live
steps.detail: In Developer Hub, click 'Change to live' on the private app. Pipedrive checks the callback URL at this point, so it must be the working Composio URL.
gotchas: A live private app can't go back to draft.
While still in draft, the app only works for users in your own Pipedrive company.

steps.title: Share the unlisted installation link
steps.detail: Get the installation link from the three-dot menu next to the app's name in Developer Hub, or from the 'Share app' button. Send it to users in any Pipedrive company, or have them connect through your Composio flow.

steps.title: (Optional, Marketplace only) Prepare the public app listing and compliance materials
steps.detail: For a separate public app, draft the listing (short summary up to 150 characters, description up to 1500 characters, a 1:1 icon of at least 256x256, and 1-5 images at 16:10), Terms of Service and Privacy Policy pages, installation and onboarding instructions, a pricing page link and support contact details. Remove any scopes you don't need.
gotchas: Your app must not collect users' API tokens; Marketplace apps must use OAuth 2.0.

steps.title: (Optional) Record the demo video and submit for review
steps.detail: Agree to the Developer Partner Agreement, record a demo video explaining how the app uses each scope and its key features, and provide working test accounts and a contact person. Then preview the listing and click 'Send to review'.

steps.title: Wait for Marketplace review
steps.detail: Public app reviews can take up to 21 business days. If the app is rejected, you'll get an email with the reasons, and you must fix them before resubmitting.

steps.title: Publish the approved app
steps.detail: Approved apps are unlisted by default. Click 'Publish' to make the app visible in the Marketplace.

requirements.item: Developer sandbox account with Developer Hub access
requirements.detail: Choose 'I'm building an app that integrates with Pipedrive' when you sign up.

requirements.item: App name and a single OAuth Callback URL
requirements.detail: Only one callback URL is allowed per app, so set it to the Composio callback.

requirements.item: Working callback URL before going live
requirements.detail: Pipedrive checks the callback URL when you click 'Change to live'.

requirements.item: Developer Partner Agreement, Terms of Service page, Privacy Policy page
requirements.detail: Legal requirements for public Marketplace apps.

requirements.item: Demo video, test accounts, contact person
requirements.detail: The demo video must explain how the app uses its permissions and scopes.
A unique name, an icon (1:1, at least 256x256, at most 10 MB), 1-5 images at 16:10 (3-5 expected), a pricing link, support contact details, and installation and onboarding guides.
Use OAuth 2.0, never collect API tokens, refresh tokens after 60 minutes, request only the scopes you need, test install and uninstall, and respect rate limits.

scopes.scope: contacts:full, leads:full, mail:full, activities:full, products:full, projects:full
scopes.effect: Composio's default scopes. Select them on the app in Developer Hub, not in Composio. They only matter for review if you submit a public app, where you must justify each one in the demo video.
Grants broad admin rights (pipelines, fields, users and permissions, webhooks). Pipedrive documents no separate tier for it, but Marketplace reviewers expect you to request only the scopes you need.

blockers.symptom: Users outside your company can't install or authorize the app
blockers.cause: The private app is still in draft. Draft private apps only work for users in the same Pipedrive company.
blockers.fix: Click 'Change to live' in Developer Hub and share the unlisted installation link.

blockers.symptom: 'Change to live' fails or the OAuth callback errors out
blockers.cause: The callback URL doesn't work or doesn't match Composio's callback. Only one URL is allowed per app.
blockers.fix: Set the OAuth Callback URL to exactly the callback shown in your Composio auth config, then try again.

blockers.cause: The client_id is invalid or wrong.
blockers.fix: Copy the client_id and client_secret again from the 'OAuth & access scopes' tab into the Composio auth config.

blockers.symptom: You can't find Developer Hub in Settings
blockers.cause: The account isn't a developer sandbox, or you didn't choose the app-building option at sign-up.
blockers.fix: Sign up for a sandbox at developers.pipedrive.com and choose 'I'm building an app that integrates with Pipedrive'.

blockers.symptom: Connections stop working after a long idle period
blockers.cause: The refresh token expires after 60 days without use.
blockers.fix: Have users reconnect, or make sure tokens are refreshed regularly.

blockers.cause: Missing legal pages, an unexplained or unnecessary scope, a missing demo video or test accounts, or a listing that doesn't meet the requirements.
blockers.fix: Fix every reason listed in the email, then resubmit with 'Send to review'.

composio.note: Composio has no managed OAuth app for Pipedrive, so you either register your own app or use Composio's API_KEY mode (a personal API token). For an agent, a live private app is enough: there's no review, and any Pipedrive company can install it. Set the app's only callback URL to the callback shown in your Composio auth config. Scopes are fixed on the Pipedrive app, so select Composio's default scopes in Developer Hub.

evidence.claim: Composio toolkit 'pipedrive' supports OAUTH2 and API_KEY modes, with no managed OAuth; it lists the authorize and token URLs and the default scopes.
The developer portal offers sign-up for a Sandbox Account for development.
evidence.quote: Sign up for a Sandbox Account today to begin experimenting and developing in a risk free environment

evidence.claim: A developer sandbox account is required to see Developer Hub, which is under Settings > (company name) > Developer Hub.
evidence.quote: You must have a developer sandbox account for app creation to see Developer Hub.

evidence.claim: At sandbox sign-up, select the app-building option to get Developer Hub access.
evidence.quote: make sure you select the option "I'm building an app that integrates with Pipedrive" as this option gives you access to the Developer Hub

evidence.claim: Developer Hub is available in all developer sandbox accounts.
evidence.quote: From today, Developer Hub will be available in all developer sandbox accounts.

evidence.claim: Apps are created via 'Create an app' as public or private, and the app type can't be changed later.
evidence.quote: NB: Do pick your app type carefully, as it cannot be changed later on Developer Hub.

evidence.claim: Basic info requires App name and OAuth Callback URL; client_id and client_secret appear on the 'OAuth & access scopes' tab.
evidence.quote: This tab has two required fields – App name and OAuth Callback URL.

evidence.claim: Only one callback URL is allowed per app.
evidence.quote: Please keep in mind that we allow only one callback URL per app.

evidence.claim: Scopes are set on the app in Developer Hub, and users accept or deny all scopes together.
evidence.quote: The user has the option to either **accept or deny all scopes**.

evidence.claim: Draft apps can be tested with the 'Install & test' button.
evidence.quote: You can do so by clicking on the green “Install & test” button in the bottom left of the tab.

evidence.claim: Private apps can be shared with any Pipedrive company via an unlisted installation link.
evidence.quote: Private apps, aka internal apps, enable you to share your integration with any user/company in Pipedrive via a direct, unlisted installation link.

evidence.claim: 'Change to live' checks the callback URL; live private apps can't revert to draft, and draft private apps are limited to the same company.
evidence.quote: As we will validate your callback URL when you click “Change to live”, please **ensure your OAuth callback URL is a functioning one**.

evidence.claim: The installation link is in the three-dot menu or behind the 'Share app' button.
evidence.quote: The installation link can be found in the three-dot menu next to your private app’s name in your Developer Hub dashboard.

evidence.claim: Marketplace submission is unnecessary for internal use; a private app can be used instead.
evidence.quote: Submitting the app is unnecessary if it’s only used internally. You can instead [create a Private app]

evidence.claim: Public app reviews may take up to 21 business days.
evidence.quote: public app reviews may take up to 21 business days

evidence.claim: Approval steps end with clicking 'Send to review'.
evidence.quote: Click on “Send to review”

evidence.claim: Public apps need the Developer Partner Agreement plus Terms of Service and Privacy Policy pages.
evidence.quote: Your app has a Privacy Policy webpage of a legal document with most or all the information on how users’ data is gathered, used, communicated and managed

evidence.claim: Reviewers require a demo video explaining scope usage, test accounts and a contact person.
evidence.quote: Provide our team with a demo video in which you explain the usage of permissions and scopes

evidence.claim: Technical requirements include OAuth 2.0, no API token collection, token refresh, minimal scopes and respecting rate limits.
evidence.quote: Your app does not collect, store, or unnecessarily use the [API token] of a user

evidence.claim: Listing requirements include a unique name, an icon, 3-5 images, a pricing link, support contacts and installation and onboarding guides.
evidence.quote: Your app listing includes **3-5 high-quality images**

evidence.claim: Rejections are emailed with reasons; approved apps are unlisted by default until published.
evidence.quote: The app is unlisted from the Marketplace by default after approval.

evidence.claim: Listing asset specs: icon 1:1, at least 256x256, at most 10 MB; images 16:10; description length limits.
evidence.quote:
– min 256x256 px
– max 10 MB

evidence.claim: The authorize request takes client_id, redirect_uri (which must match the registered value) and an optional state.
evidence.quote: GET https://oauth.pipedrive.com/oauth/authorize?client_id=b4d083d9216986345b32&state=148aHxbdd92&redirect_uri=https://awesomeapp.com/oauth/callback

evidence.claim: The authorization code expires in 5 minutes; the token exchange uses HTTP Basic auth.
evidence.quote: Note that the `authorization_code` expires in **5 minutes**.

evidence.claim: Refresh tokens expire after 60 days without use; access tokens expire after 60 minutes; the token response includes api_domain.
evidence.quote: `refresh_token` will expire if it isn't used in **60 days**. Each time `refresh_token` is used, its expiry date is **reset** back to **60 days**.

evidence.claim: The available scopes include base (always enabled), contacts, leads, mail, activities, products, projects, deals, admin and others.
evidence.quote: ⚠️ *This is the default permission that is always enabled for all apps.*

evidence.claim: The admin scope grants broad admin capabilities; no separate sensitive tier is documented.
evidence.quote: Allows to do many things that an administrator can do in a Pipedrive company account

evidence.claim: An invalid client_id on the authorize endpoint returns a 401 JSON error.
evidence.quote: {"success":false,"error":"unauthorized access","errorCode":401,"error_info":"Please check developers.pipedrive.com"}

evidence.claim: Rate limits are token-based and apply per Pipedrive company account, not per app.
evidence.quote: Each Pipedrive company account gets a daily token budget calculated as 30,000 base tokens × plan multiplier × number of seats.

evidence.claim: OAuth 2.0 is required for Marketplace apps.
evidence.quote: Using OAuth 2.0 is necessary for developing apps that are available in the Pipedrive Marketplace.

open_questions: Which Composio callback URL to register: sources list both https://backend.composio.dev/api/v1/auth-apps/add and https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3/toolkits/auth/callback. Use the one your Composio auth config shows, since Pipedrive allows only one.
Not confirmed whether a draft private app can authorize a real (non-sandbox) Pipedrive account you own in another company. The docs suggest you must go live first.
No install caps are documented for live private apps.
Whether the sandbox account is free or time-limited isn't confirmed on an official page.
The rate-limit figures come from third-party sources, not Pipedrive's official rate-limit page.
